I have farmed this land for 55 years. I know this soil, I know this weather, and I know what my body can still handle at 78. My wife and I are the only two workers on this farm. I cannot afford to make mistakes — we depend on what comes out of this ground.

My 4.1 mu is split the way it has always been: about 2.5 mu on the wheat-maize rotation, and the remaining 1.6 mu in cotton. I thought about cutting the cotton this year because picking is hard on my back and cotton needs a lot of hands at harvest. But cotton is cash. Wheat and maize feed us and feed the animals; cotton pays the bills. I will keep the cotton but I will not expand it.

**Wheat (winter):** I sow in October after the soil is prepared. I use improved seed — the Jimai varieties work well here, the extension station has been pushing them for years and my neighbors get good results. I apply compound fertilizer as base and come back with urea at jointing. Three irrigations: one before winter sets in, one at jointing, one at grain filling. Two pesticide passes — herbicide in early winter, then something for rust and aphids near heading. I use rotary tillage; deep ploughing is too tiring at my age and the rotary gets the job done fine.

**Maize (summer):** Right after I harvest wheat in June, I seed maize directly into the stubble. No tillage — I have done this for years now and yields are the same, and it saves me a full day of work. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the seed shop recommends this season. Two irrigations — one to get it established, one at silking if rain does not come. Two pesticide applications: herbicide early, then something for corn borer. I apply fertilizer mostly as topdress at the big-bell stage.

**Cotton:** I transplant seedlings in late April or early May. I use Bt hybrid cotton — the insect pressure is lower than it used to be with the old varieties and I do not have to spray as many times. Four irrigations across the season. Four pesticide applications — I still watch carefully for aphids and bollworms even with Bt. I plough this plot properly before transplanting.
